<a id="acid_rain"></a>
## Acid House: `acid_rain.yml`

Acid house in A minor at 126 beats a minute, every part on the built-in
synths, written to show [Fishline](../synths/engines/FISHLINE.md). The squelch
is Fishline's saw through its Diode filter, deep and resonant, its Acid gate
set to Modded so that a run of accents climbs higher. The lead is Fishline's
square two octaves over it, and an octave higher still at the peak, to show
the instrument's whole range. MechaDrum plays the synth kick, snare, hats and
cowbell.

The squelch hardly changes its notes; what moves is its marks, and they are
rare: two accents a bar, off the beat and after a rest, and one slide a bar
into the octave jump. Every second bar moves its accents and adds a slide, and
the last bar of each eight climbs through three accents, the turnaround. The
lead is a two-bar call and answer whose long note is its peak. The intro is
two bars, the second drop lifts everything a fourth, and the peak takes the
lead an octave up.

<a id="duck_blur"></a>
## 8-Bit Game Theme: `duck_blur.yml`

A bright, fast 8-bit game theme in the manner of the DuckTales theme (Mark
Mueller), as a console of the eighties played it, every part on the built-in
synths: a square lead with a little vibrato, a two-oscillator chord stab, a
triangle bass bouncing octaves, and MechaDrum's kick, snare and hats. The
verse's busy patter of repeated notes is answered by short tags; the lift
climbs in two parallel lines while its snare rolls into the chorus; and the
chorus opens each half with two punchy notes and a high answer before a long
running line, over the borrowed chords bVI and bVII rising to I. A stuttering
bridge of calls and answers comes before the last two choruses. The chords of
every scene come from the [Chords](../generators/CHORDS.md) generator on the
chords and bass tracks.

<a id="cartridge_quest"></a>
## Chip Adventure Theme: `cartridge_quest.yml`

A home-computer adventure theme in D minor at 150 beats a minute, every sound
on the [SID](../synths/engines/SID.md) engine, as one sound chip of the 1980s
played it. The lead is a pulse wave whose width an LFO sweeps slowly through
the Mod Matrix, with a second LFO adding vibrato. The arpeggio plays each
chord as a single note, and the oscillator's Arpeggio steps it through root,
fifth and octave fifty times a second, the chip composer's way of sounding a
chord on one voice. A triangle plays the bass, the chip's noise wave the snare
and hats, a triangle with a falling pitch the kick, and a ring-modulated
triangle is a bell that answers the lead.

The verse and the chorus differ in every way a chip can make them differ. The
verse sits low, on a two-bar motif stated four times with its ending changed,
its chords two bars each, with no snare, a dark arpeggio and soft notes. The
pre-chorus climbs a step a bar while a noise roll speeds up. The chorus jumps
an octave to its hook, a chord a bar, a backbeat, a bright arpeggio and loud
notes. The [Phrasing](../generators/PHRASING.md) generator shapes the lead's
lines, each growing toward its long note and breathing after it.

<a id="side_pocket"></a>
## Chip Funk: `side_pocket.yml`

Chip funk in E dorian at 104 beats a minute, every sound on the
[Pocket](../synths/engines/POCKET.md) engine, a handheld game console's sound
chip. Funk is in what is left out: everyone hits the one hard, every part is
short and mostly rests, each fitting into the others' holes, and the
sixteenths swing only lightly. The snare's backbeat is answered by ghost
notes, the bass plays short notes around rests, and the two pulse channels
play the chords as stabs of two guide tones, mostly ghosts. It also shows the
Mod Matrix's MIDI CC sources: a CC row sent as CC 74 rides the stabs' cutoff
through every beat, a wah, opens the bass's filter over the groove, and in
the solo CC 1, the mod wheel, brings vibrato in late on each held note of the
hook's pulse channel.

<a id="machine_room"></a>
## Drum Machine Jam: `machine_room.yml`

A drum machine jam at 122 beats a minute on
[MechaDrum](../synths/engines/MECHADRUM.md), the built-in drum machine, each
of its ten machines heard, with no lead and no chords: the groove is the
music. The sixteenths swing a little, so the hats, the rim and the snare's
ghost notes shuffle while the kick stays on the beat. The kick is loudest on
the one, with a Hard Kick layered under it, the snare answers its backbeat
with ghost notes, the rim plays a clave over two bars and the Karplus Drum a
conga part on the root and the fifth. The closed and open hats are one
machine in one choke group, so each closed hit cuts the open one short. The
Acoustic Tom fills only the last bar of each eight, and the drop swaps the
kick for the Hard Kick's broken electro pattern.
